title: fix(service-datasource): a runtime managed datasource syncs its bound objects' tables on create and after a restart
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D1H8LKUgLcNior93UM4jPpL)_

domain:server#3 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czbMpdApCUbUuNyHt7

Fixes #27701

## What changes

- `registerPool` (`packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts`) now opens a runtime datasource's pool with `objects`: the names of the objects bound to it in the engine registry. The connect's existing sync loop gives them their tables. This covers the admin create, the boot rehydration, and a peer replica's convergence on a new datasource, which all go through `registerPool`.
- ⛔ The objects are passed only when the datasource is managed. Its mode is read with `resolveDatasourceSchemaMode`, the same read the driver factory uses. An `external` or `validate-only` datasource passes none and never gets DDL (triage ruling `6506923793`).
- The registry read that `listObjectsBoundTo` already did is lifted into one local helper, `objectsBoundTo`, which both readers call. `listObjectsBoundTo`'s answer is byte-for-byte the same.
- Neither `datasource-connection-service.ts` (open PR #27715) nor `objectql/src/engine.ts` is touched.

## Why

A code object bound to a Setup-created managed datasource never got its table. Boot's schema sync skipped it, because the driver did not exist yet. `registerPool` then called `connect(record, { context })` with no `objects`, so the sync loop had nothing to sync. The datasource answered `ok`, and every read of the object was a 500 (Postgres `42P01`), the same after a restart.

## Verification

New pin: `src/__tests__/runtime-datasource-bound-object-storage.test.ts`. It uses the real `DatasourceAdminServicePlugin` through `init()` and `start()`, a real `ObjectQL` engine on the `objectql` and `data` slots, and the real default driver factory over SQLite files.

| Case | `origin/main` plugin | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| on create, the bound object's table exists and the object reads | red | green |
| after a restart, the rehydrated pool creates a missing table and the object reads | red | green |
| control: an object bound to another datasource is not synced | red | green |
| ⛔ `schemaMode: external`: the pool opens, nothing is synced | green | green |
| ⛔ `schemaMode: validate-only`: the pool opens, nothing is synced | green | green |

Ablations, each restored afterwards:
- Dropping the `objects` argument turns the 3 positive cases red.
- Forcing the managed gate open turns both negative cases red (`syncObjectSchema` called 2 times).

Local readings at `6f773675`:
- `@objectstack/service-datasource` `test`: 62 files, 1016/1016 passed. `typecheck`: exit 0.
- `dispatch-gates --commands`: 59 families derived, 58 exit 0. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3, so it is NOT MEASURED (it needs a whole-tree build; CI runs it).
- `dispatch-gates --ran`: 59 accounted for.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, measured (class a).** An edit that rebuilds the pool still syncs nothing. That covers a changed `config`, credential, `schemaMode` or `active` (`updateDatasource` → `reregisterPool` → `DatasourceConnectionService.reconnect`). `reconnect` takes no `objects`, and its inner `connect(record, { context })` is in `datasource-connection-service.ts`.
  - Measured with the same rig: create `warehouse` on `a.db`, then update its `config` to `b.db`. The result is `hasTable('wh_note') === false`, and the read is refused by the database.
  - `reach:` the admin update door (`PATCH /api/v1/datasources/:name` → `updateDatasource`). The fix belongs in the connection service, serial behind #27715.
- A federated object (`external` set) on a managed datasource would go through `syncObjectSchema`'s DDL-free `registerExternalObject` branch. The admin door already refuses that binding at write time (#25277).
